title: Email change with confirmation
description:
People can edit their display name but not their address: today an operator has to change `users.email` by hand. This adds a self-service change that is confirmed from the new mailbox.

- `POST /v1/me/email {new_email, password}` (access token) asks for the password again (403 `permission_denied` when it is wrong) and answers 202 with `{new_email, expires_at}`. It stores a pending change with only the SHA-256 of a random token, like refresh tokens and invitations, valid for `EMAIL_CHANGE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 24 h), then emails `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/account/email/confirm?token=…` to the new address and a notice naming the new address to the current one. The emails go out after the commit, as for invitations. The answer does not depend on whether the new address already has an account: availability is only checked on confirmation, by someone who has shown they read that mailbox. The current address itself is a 422. Requests are limited per user (`EMAIL_CHANGE_RATE_LIMIT` per `EMAIL_CHANGE_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS`, default 5 per hour), counted before the password is checked, so a stolen access token is worth at most that many password guesses.
- `POST /v1/me/email/confirm {token}` needs an access token of the account that asked, so a link opened by anyone else does nothing. It switches the address and returns the profile. A link of another account answers 404 like an unknown one (and is not spent), an already used link 409, an expired one 410, and 409 when another account has taken the address meanwhile. Confirmation needs no throttle of its own: the token carries 256 bits and the route needs the account's own token.
- Concurrency: requests and confirmations of one user lock the user row first, so they run one at a time; a new request deletes the user's unconfirmed change, so only the newest link works. Uniqueness is left to the existing case-insensitive unique index on `lower(email)`: `UserRepository.set_email` updates inside a savepoint and turns the unique violation into a 409, which covers two accounts confirming one address and a confirmation racing an account creation.
- Sessions stay signed in; the next login uses the new address and the old one stops working. Pending invitations are not transferred: they stay addressed to the old address, so the account can no longer accept them, and invitations already sent to the new address become acceptable. The audit log is per organisation, so the change is logged (`user.email_change_requested`, `user.email_changed`, with ids only, never the token) rather than audited.
- Migration 0006 adds `email_changes` (`user_id`, normalised `new_email`, unique `token_hash`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `used_at`), `EmailChange`, `EmailChangeRepository` and `EmailChangeService`; settings, `.env.example` and README updated. Test helper: `RecordingMailer.last_email_change_token(address)`.

Tests: `tests/api/test_email_change.py` (address switched and logins follow it, notice to the old address without the token, password required again, current address refused, taken address refused only on confirmation, newest link only, single use, links of other accounts, expiry, per-user rate limit).
